sourceMethods: All 128 active subnet profiles and 98 September 16–17 dated channel briefs reviewed; previous editions checked for duplicate events and late recaps.

175 public X account candidates sampled (164 returned linked posts), producing 185 deduplicated current post records. Candidates include projects, aliases, partners and commentators, not just verified official accounts.

Signed-in X broad and targeted searches, SN44 Score’s original profile, the Crucible release thread and a Grok scan were reviewed; new Grok leads were followed to original sources. External-source checks included OpenTensor, ForeverMoney, BaseStonk, StonkFun, Sunrise, Bankr and Chainlink.
Signed-in AlphaGap Feed and leaderboard checked, plus SubnetRadar, TAO Daily, TAO Media and the public project-news feed. Conflicting or stale summary claims were checked against dated originals.
164 repository paths scanned and refreshed; selected implementation patches, release notes and the merged runtime 464 pull request inspected.
19 unique linked SubnetRadar Moments in the coverage window reviewed, with original event timestamps and text retained.
Network allocation and rolling alpha/TAO prices observed at 10:56 AM ET and compared with the September 16 saved snapshot.

Public product and evidence pages checked for SN44 Score Studio, SN66 Conjectures proofs and independent problem status, SN28 SayGM burns, SN41 Almanac’s dated ledger, SN19 Blockmachine reserve and SN8 Vanta Pro accounts. The September 16 StonkFun table row was verified in the browser.

YouTube Videos and Live listings checked; the September 16 members video’s title, 10:12 listing duration, membership gate and publication timestamp were verified. Owner-removed promotions and replays remain excluded.
accessGaps: All 128 active subnet profiles were reviewed and linked public X account candidates sampled, supplemented by selected signed-in searches and Grok. This is not a guarantee that every post was found; private, deleted, unindexed and unsampled material may be absent.

Private Discord was not directly accessed. Brief-only operational claims retain digest attribution and developing labels. AlphaGap was used for discovery, not as independent proof of deployment, revenue or wallet intent.

SN66 Conjectures published both Lean proof files and reports verification. The independent Erdős Problems directory still marks #14 open. This scan did not rerun Lean or independently adjudicate the mathematics.

Network emission allocation is compared between saved snapshots. It is distinct from miner reward payments, burn weights and voluntary owner actions. No cause or administrative switch is inferred from the allocation changes.

Runtime 464 is merged but was not independently confirmed active on Finney. Basket trading remains gated off in the merged change. Subnet implementation merges do not establish adoption by every validator.

SN41 Almanac’s revenue display mirrors buyback dollars without a separate fee feed. SN19 Blockmachine’s announcement changes a policy whose older wording remains on its ledger. SN28 SayGM’s $43K burn valuation is team-reported; the ledger records 9,523 alpha and 13.0% cycle coverage.

SN8 Vanta’s reward announcement reports newer totals than the initially rendered public ledger; those mismatched totals were excluded. All account capital described is simulated and promotion is discretionary. SN14 Cacheon explicitly says benchmark test conditions differ.

SN78 UMI’s Convo meeting is exploratory and its congressional-office contact is not a government contract. Competition admission does not establish payment. SN74 Gittensor’s checked compute release-channel documentation says the agent image/manifest has not yet been published.

Automatically generated Moments interpretations about smart money, validator identity and supply shares were not accepted as proof. SN55 NIOME migration articles, SN61 RedTeam banking coverage, SN33 ReadyAI’s app and the initial SN126 Attelier rebrand were deduplicated against prior editions.
8 repository paths had an access or refresh error; details are retained in the audit. Sources were checked at different times, with the final code/market pass through 10:57 AM ET.

editorialDecisions.decision: Five stars for the public Studio launch and SN28 inference integration confirmed by both parties. Custom bounty burns are attributed to OpenTensor. Future Studio-profit burns are plans, with no newly disclosed revenue or completed burn totals.

Five stars, developing: this is Erdős 14, distinct from the earlier Erdős 96 announcement. Both public Lean source files were inspected but not executed. The independent problem directory still labels the problem open. Price observations use alpha/TAO and do not establish causation.
Cycle 01 records 9,523 alpha burned against 73,193 miner emissions, or 13.0% coverage. The approximately $43,000 valuation is team-reported. The separate SN44 story covers the inference integration.

The original X dollar figure is malformed. The dated September 16 ledger confirms $24,771 and 22,284.5 alpha bought and burned, September buybacks of $40,689.01 and cumulative buybacks of $116,901.31. The displayed revenue mirrors buybacks without an independent fee feed. The September 8 purchase remains held.

The team reports a reserve burn of 67.7 TAO, valued at $15,612. Its $3,964.79 buyback announcement differs slightly from the ledger’s $3,967.94, so the story uses approximately $4,000. The ledger records 1,801.09 alpha purchased and a zero reserve balance. Older reserve-policy wording conflicts with the new announcement.

Pro accounts are supported by the official offer and implementation. Capital is simulated and promotion discretionary. Conflicting reward totals from the announcement and initially rendered ledger were excluded.

The team reports 1,242.8 tokens per second and a roughly 12.5% comparison under different conditions. This is not a controlled benchmark comparison. Its own mining participation is disclosed in the original announcement.

The first intake is live, but an accepted_no_weight receipt does not activate competition rewards. The registration reopening and 0.75 TAO fee are digest-attributed. Convo talks are exploratory; congressional outreach is not a government contract or endorsement.

The phase-one compute implementation is merged, but release documentation says the agent image and stable manifest have not yet been published. The story describes groundwork, not a completed public rollout.

Runtime 464 merged at 11:52:45 UTC. Basket trading remains gated off and the PR does not start a release train. Its authors describe Finney as running 459 at the time of writing. No causal link to subnet allocation changes is asserted. The StonkFun September 16 table verifies platform-wide figures of $561,373 revenue, $335,379 buybacks and 2.06 million STONK burned.

Crucible was discovered through TAO Daily, then verified against its signed-in X original. Bankr’s TAO pair was already covered on September 10. Chainlink’s Bottomline announcement is not a new TAO integration. No new const or arbos announcement was found in the sampled public posts.
A commentator’s URnetwork mainnet claim was not confirmed from a current primary announcement and was omitted as a fresh launch.
The NIOME interview repeats a Q4 migration and conviction-swap plan already covered on September 10; it was excluded as a recap.

The final repository refresh found five dependency merges and a benchmark documentation correction in synthdataco/synth-lib. The latter clarifies underlying-market seasonality in perpetual-price data. No new launch or changed scoring rule was established, so these routine updates were not added as another news item.
